config_name: XPS 16 — Core Ultra 7 355, 16GB LPDDR5X, 1TB SSD, 16" FHD+ 120Hz non-touch

specs.cpu: Intel Core Ultra 7 355 (Series 3 Panther Lake, 8-core, up to 4.7 GHz)
specs.ports: 3x Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) with DP 2.1 + PD, universal audio jack
specs.keyboard_notes: Backlit keyboard, zero-lattice design, Gorilla Glass 3 palmrest

battery.notes: 70Wh. Dell claims up to 31h streaming on 2K display @250 nits; real-world mixed ~11-13h.

price.notes: VERIFIED dell.ca 2026-11-24: CAD $3,899.99. Note: the 358H/Arc config below is $300 CHEAPER — Dell pricing anomaly.

reviews.quote: the XPS 16 is a fantastic laptop befitting of the premium XPS name

praises: Dell's thinnest 16-inch: 14.6-15.4 mm and 1.74 kg — lighter than most 14-inch laptops from three years ago
Up to 31h claimed streaming on this exact 2K LCD config; class-leading battery
1TB standard even at entry tier, unlike the XPS 14 base
3x TB4 with DP 2.1 handles triple-monitor docking
Sleek CNC aluminum design owners describe as premium in every review
complaints: 16GB soldered at a CAD $3,900 price is stingy; the better-spec'd 358H config is actually cheaper
FHD+ 1200p on 16 inches is visibly low-density; most buyers should skip this tier
No HDMI/SD/USB-A — the old XPS 16 ports returned only on Creator Edition (CNET con: limited ports)
8-core 355 lacks Arc iGPU punch of the 358H tiers

design_philosophy: The 2026 XPS 16 rebuild abandons the 2025 Premium's throttled RTX dGPU in favour of extreme thinness and battery — 'the ultimate creator's canvas... in our thinnest 16-inch laptop' per Dell. This entry tier is the battery-maximalist door, though Dell's own pricing makes it hard to recommend over the mid tier.
rating_notes: Inferred from CNET XPS 16 (2026) 8.0 anchor (US$2,650 as-reviewed). Entry tier with weaker 8-core CPU: productivity −0.5, gaming −1 vs Arc tiers. screen_size 8.5 for 16"; portability 8.0 (1.74 kg is light for 16").
